# Header Check via `head -5` Misses Frontmatter Files

**Date**: 2026-05-24
**PR**: PR98
**Category**: wrong-validation

## What Happened

While planning PR98, we needed to find all `.jp.md` files in the repository
that were missing the standard JP-mirror warning comment
(`<!-- This file is a Japanese mirror. ... -->`).

The initial check looked at the first 5 lines of each file:

```bash
find . -name "*.jp.md" | while read f; do
  if ! head -5 "$f" | grep -q "<!-- This file is a Japanese mirror"; then
    echo "MISSING: $f"
  fi
done
```

This reported **39 files** missing the warning. We then planned the backfill
based on that number — categorized the files, sized the changelogs, etc.

Only when actually opening some of those "missing" files did we notice that
they did have the warning — just not in the first 5 lines, because of YAML
frontmatter:

```
---
name: pr-handoff
description: |
  ...
---
<!-- Generated by claude-kit/skill-creator v3.17.1 -->
<!-- This file is a Japanese mirror. When updating the English original, update this file too. -->
```

The warning sits at line 7+, not lines 1–5. The `head -5` check missed it.

The real number of files truly missing the warning was **25**, not 39.

## Root Cause

`head -5` checks the first 5 lines of a file regardless of structure.
For files with frontmatter, those 5 lines are mostly the frontmatter itself,
leaving zero or one lines of actual body content. The metadata comment that
follows the frontmatter is never inspected.

## Fix Applied

When verifying file-header metadata across mixed-structure markdown files,
parse and skip the YAML frontmatter first, then inspect the first few lines
of the body. A Python check that handles this:

```python
text = file.read_text()
body = text
if text.startswith('---\n'):
    end = text.find('\n---\n', 4)
    if end != -1:
        body = text[end+5:]
lines = body.splitlines()
head = '\n'.join(lines[:5])
# now grep the body head for the marker
```

This produced the correct count of 25 missing files.

## Lesson

When validating file-position-specific metadata across a heterogeneous set
of files (some with frontmatter, some without), simple line-count tools
like `head -N` are insufficient. The validation script must:

- Recognize frontmatter (`---` ... `---`) and skip it
- Inspect the first few lines of the body, not the file

This is especially relevant for backfill operations, where overcounting
"missing" files leads to wrong scope, wrong changelogs, and wasted setup time.
